text_blocks.snippet: Reactine is an over-the-counter medication that provides relief from allergy symptoms. It contains the active ingredient cetirizine, a second-generation antihistamine that works by blocking histamine, a chemical released during an allergic reaction. Reactine is commonly used to treat symptoms like itchy, watery eyes, runny nose, sneezing, and itchy throat and skin.
snippet_highlighted_words: an over-the-counter medication that provides relief from allergy symptoms

list.title: Mechanism of Action:
list.snippet: Reactine (cetirizine) is an antihistamine that works by blocking histamine, a chemical that the body releases in response to allergens (like pollen, dust, or pet dander).

list.title: Uses:
list.snippet: It's used to relieve allergy symptoms such as:

list.title: Forms and Dosage:
list.snippet: Reactine is available in various forms, including tablets, liquid gels, and orally disintegrating tablets. The dosage for adults and children 12 years and older is usually 1 or 2 tablets (or equivalent) every 24 hours. It's always best to follow the instructions on the packaging or consult a doctor or pharmacist for specific dosage recommendations.

list.title: Side Effects:
list.snippet: Common side effects can include drowsiness or dizziness. Other potential side effects, as noted by Cleveland Clinic, may include dry mouth.

list.title: Where to Buy:
list.snippet: Reactine is readily available over-the-counter at most pharmacies and drugstores.
